content.title: Eid Al Fitr 2026: When is Eid? check correct date and significance
content.text: One of the most well-known Muslim festivals is Eid. Eid is celebrated twice a year - Eid Ul Fitar and Eid Ul Adha. The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and fervor across the globe, where Muslim community lives. Eid ul fitr is celebrated in March- April month following the Islamic calendar. Eid al-Fitr 2026 is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic Hijri calendar. This is also known as meethi Eid. This event is observed by people from various nations with their friends, family, and relatives. They express their joy and celebrate this festival with immense happiness. The Islamic calendar's ninth month, Ramadan concludes with Eid Ul Fitr. These five principles are considered to be especially important to observe on this festival in Islam. This covers fasting, zakat, faith, offering namaz, and the Hajj journey. The first known Eid celebration is believed to have occurred around 624 AD. The Prophet Muhammad established Eid ul Fitr. Prophet Hazrat Muhammad is supposed to have won the Battle of Badr on this historical day. Sweets were distributed as a way to celebrate the Prophet's accomplishment. The day is celebrated by cooking a wide variety of foods. Before Bakrid, Meethi Eid is celebrated every year. Muslims celebrate this to conclude the Ramadan and show gratitude to Allah.Eid Al Fitr: CelebrationOne of the mos prominent Muslim festivals is Eid Ul Fitr, which is celebrated magnificently by Muslims all around the globe. They pray to Allah, cook delicious food, invite friends and family to their homes, and travel to their locations or home towns. Before beginning rituals, they take a holy bath after waking up early in the morning. They offer their first prayer in the morning and express their gratitude to Allah once they complete bathing ritual. Following this, women participate in the preparation of various food items and desserts, which is the main part of this festival. Men go to the mosque, pray to Allah specifically, and seek blessings. On this auspicious day, people can also ask the Almighty for forgiveness if they have made any mistakes throughout the month-long fast.Muslims celebrate this day with great happiness and fervor and break their fast with dates and water. They host lunch or dinner, invite their friends and family to their house, and even pay them a visit. Give gifts and sweets to one another. Youngsters ask their elders for their Eidi. People participate in giving food, clothing, water, and cash to those in need because it is seen to be an auspicious day to do so. To express their joy, women wear new traditional outfits and apply mehendi.
